chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from Abī Ayyūb, from Ḥarīz, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who killed another man intentionally, then was delivered to the governor, and the governor handed him over to the heirs of the slain so that they might kill him. Then some people attacked them and rescued the killer from the hands of the heirs. He said: “I hold that those who rescued the killer from the hands of the heirs should be imprisoned until they produce the killer.” It was said: “Then if the killer dies while they are in prison?” He said: “If he dies, then the blood money is upon them.”

key_terms.أَوْلِيَاءِ الْمَقْتُولِ: the heirs or legal claimants of the slain person who possess the right of retaliation
key_terms.الدِّيَةُ: the blood money owed as financial compensation for a life
key_terms.السِّجْنِ: the prison in which the rescuers are held
key_terms.الْقَاتِلَ: the killer or murderer subject to retaliation
key_terms.الْوَالِي: the governing authority or ruler responsible for enforcing legal judgments

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on those who rescue an intentional killer from the heirs of the victim before retaliation is carried out?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning people who interfere with the lawful execution of retaliation against an intentional killer after he has been handed over to the slain person’s heirs. It states that those who rescue the killer are to be detained until they bring him back, and if the killer dies before that, they become liable for the blood money.
